docs.title: 22 — React & Tailwind: versions, architecture and the model to train
docs.text:
Last verified: 25 October 2026. Version facts were checked against the npm registry, React and Tailwind release posts, the TypeScript 7 announcement, the Vite 8 announcement, the React Router v8 changelog and Node's release index.

If you want one Qwen3 base for Kali, Java and React instead of a React-specific coder, see 26 — One Qwen3 for all. The React-specific adapter here is still the higher-quality option for React.

For a second base with native vision and 256K context, see the parallel Gemma 4 12B React track and Gemma fine-tuning. It does not replace this Qwen track.

This is the start of the front-end track. It answers the same three questions as the Java track:

  1. Which React and Tailwind versions should the model target?
  2. What does a good React/Tailwind codebase look like, concretely?
  3. Which Qwen coder can actually be fine-tuned on a 32 GB M1 Pro?

The short answers:

  • React 19.3 + Tailwind CSS 4.3 + Vite 8 + Node 24 LTS, with a TypeScript 7-compatible tsconfig but a TypeScript 6 tooling bridge for ESLint.
  • Feature-based architecture, a token-driven design system, accessible primitives, server-state discipline and tested states — not just “utility classes in JSX”.
  • Qwen2.5-Coder-14B-Instruct 4-bit QLoRA locally; Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B as teacher/judge. A text-only coder cannot see screenshots; use a VLM to turn a reference into a written design spec, then train the coder on the spec.

docs.title: 1. Which “latest” do you target?
docs.text:
The JavaScript ecosystem ships fast, and four different version axes matter: React, Tailwind, the build tool, and the type checker.

Component Latest as of 25 Oct 2026 Status Use in this handbook React / React DOM 19.3.1 (14 Oct 2026) Stable; 19.3.0 shipped 9 Sep 2026 Primary target Tailwind CSS 4.3.3 (16 Jul 2026) Stable; 4.3.0 shipped 8 May 2026 Primary target Vite 8.3.5 (21 Oct 2026) Stable; 8.0 shipped 12 Mar 2026 Primary target Node.js 24.22.1 “Krypton” (20 Oct 2026) Active LTS Primary runtime Node.js 26.12.1 (21 Oct 2026) Current, not LTS yet in this window Do not require for a training target TypeScript 7.0.2 (8 Jul 2026) Stable native compiler; 7.1 Beta 20 Oct 2026 Source/type-check target React Router 8.5.0 (19 Oct 2026) Stable; 8.0 shipped 17 Jun 2026 Routing target TanStack Query 5.104.5 Stable Server-state target Storybook 10.6.3 (20 Oct 2026) Stable; ESM-only since 10.0 Optional component workshop Vitest 5.0.5 (15 Oct 2026) Stable Unit/component tests Playwright 1.64.1 Stable E2E, screenshots, axe ESLint 10.13.0 (16 Oct 2026) Stable Lint target Motion 14.6.0 Stable Optional animation shadcn/ui current MIT component patterns Design-system reference

docs.title: 1.1 React 19.3
docs.text:
React 19.3 is a minor release with real features:

  • View Transitions are stable (<ViewTransition>), so page and list transitions can use the browser's View Transition API.
  • Fragment refs are stable.
  • browser() in React DOM helps with client-only rendering and bailouts.
  • Trusted Types support lets React pass Trusted Types objects through to DOM APIs.
  • Server Components remain stable, but their bundler/framework APIs are not semver-stable between 19.x minors. This handbook does not train a Server Components stack.

React 19 already gave us Actions, useActionState, useFormStatus, useOptimistic, use, ref as a prop, ref cleanup functions, and <Context> as a provider. Those are the patterns the model should learn.

docs.title: 1.2 Tailwind CSS 4.3
docs.text:
Tailwind 4 is CSS-first. The old tailwind.config.js + @tailwind base/components/utilities setup is not the default any more:

@import "tailwindcss";

@theme {
  --color-brand: oklch(0.58 0.19 275);
  --radius-card: 1rem;
}

Tailwind 4.3 adds:

  • first-party scrollbar utilities (scrollbar-*, scrollbar-color-*, scrollbar-gutter-*);
  • @container-size for block-size container queries (cqb/cqh);
  • zoom-* and tab-* utilities;
  • stacked and compound @variant rules;
  • new colors and logical-property utilities.

The v4 migration also renamed utilities and changed defaults. The ones that matter for training data:

v3 v4 shadow-sm shadow-xs shadow shadow-sm rounded-sm rounded-xs rounded rounded-sm blur-sm blur-xs outline-none outline-hidden (old behaviour); outline-none now really removes the outline ring (3px) ring-3; v4's ring is 1px bg-opacity-50 bg-black/50 flex-shrink-* shrink-* flex-grow-* grow-* overflow-ellipsis text-ellipsis decoration-slice / clone box-decoration-slice / clone

Also: the default border color changed from gray-200 to currentColor; @apply in CSS modules needs @reference; and the v4 browser baseline is Safari 16.4+, Chrome 111+, Firefox 128+.

Tag every example with tailwind: "3" or tailwind: "4". A model trained on a mix of @tailwind base and @import "tailwindcss" without tags will produce a plausible but broken hybrid.

docs.title: 1.3 TypeScript 7 — the tooling trap
docs.text:
TypeScript 7.0 is the Go-native compiler: 8–12× faster type-checking, lower memory, stricter defaults.

It is not a drop-in upgrade:

  • strict is on by default; module defaults to esnext.
  • target: es5, downlevelIteration, moduleResolution: node/node10, module: amd/umd/systemjs/none, and baseUrl are removed.
  • types and rootDir defaults are stricter; list your @types explicitly.
  • The programmatic compiler API is not available until 7.1. That breaks tools that import TypeScript, including typescript-eslint, some webpack loaders and ts-morph.

For this handbook:

  • Write source and tsconfig for TypeScript 7.0.2 (no baseUrl, strict, explicit types).
  • Run ESLint with the TypeScript 6 API (@typescript/typescript6 alias or a pinned typescript@6.0.3 dev dependency) until the lint stack supports 7.1.
  • Do not train a model to use removed tsconfig options; those examples will not build on a 2026 project.

docs.title: 1.4 Vite 8 and React Router 8
docs.text:
Vite 8 replaces esbuild + Rollup with Rolldown + Oxc. Most plugins work, builds are much faster, and the default browser target moved to Chrome 111 / Edge 111 / Firefox 114 / Safari 16.4. A few Rollup-only hooks and system/amd output formats are gone.

React Router 8 is ESM-only, requires Node 22+, Vite 7+, React 19+, and removed react-router-dom. Import core APIs from react-router and browser-specific utilities from react-router/dom. It has data, declarative and framework modes; this handbook targets data mode in a Vite SPA.

Do not mix React Router 7 or Remix idioms into v8 examples without a migration tag.

docs.title: 1.5 The baseline config
docs.text:
A TypeScript 7-compatible app tsconfig.json (no baseUrl, strict, explicit types):

{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "target": "ES2022",
    "lib": ["ES2023", "DOM", "DOM.Iterable"],
    "module": "preserve",
    "moduleResolution": "bundler",
    "jsx": "react-jsx",
    "strict": true,
    "noUncheckedIndexedAccess": true,
    "verbatimModuleSyntax": true,
    "isolatedModules": true,
    "skipLibCheck": true,
    "noEmit": true,
    "types": ["vite/client"],
    "rootDir": "src",
    "paths": { "@/*": ["./src/*"] }
  },
  "include": ["src"]
}

vite.config.ts:

import react from "@vitejs/plugin-react";
import tailwindcss from "@tailwindcss/vite";
import { defineConfig } from "vite";

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [react(), tailwindcss()],
});

package.json scripts:

{
  "scripts": {
    "typecheck": "tsc --noEmit",
    "lint": "eslint .",
    "test": "vitest",
    "build": "vite build",
    "preview": "vite preview",
    "e2e": "playwright test"
  }
}

For ESLint, keep a TypeScript 6 API available. The practical bridge is a separate lint workspace pinned to typescript@6.0.3, or the alias package:

{
  "devDependencies": {
    "typescript": "7.0.2",
    "@typescript/typescript6": "npm:typescript@6.0.2"
  }
}

tsc from TypeScript 7 checks the app; the lint workspace/alias supplies the 6.0 API. Do not put typescript@7 in a plugin that imports the compiler API until 7.1 ships it.

docs.title: 1.6 Why Node 24 LTS, not Node 26
docs.text: Node 24 is the active LTS in this window. Node 26 is Current. For a reproducible training and verification environment, target Node 24 LTS; it satisfies Vite 8, React Router 8 and Storybook 10. Mention Node 26 as an optional future upgrade.

docs.title: 2. Why a Vite SPA, not Next.js
docs.text:
“React and Tailwind” can mean many stacks. This handbook deliberately fixes one:

React 19.3 + TypeScript 7 + Vite 8 + Tailwind 4.3
React Router 8 (data mode) + TanStack Query 5
Radix primitives + shadcn/ui patterns + CVA + tailwind-merge
Vitest 5 + Testing Library + Playwright 1.64 + axe-core

Why:

  • The target is front-end UI engineering, not full-stack React.
  • A Vite SPA has one rendering model: client components. Server Components, server actions, route handlers and next/* imports would add a second, conflicting vocabulary.
  • Vite is the common base for React Router, Storybook, Vitest and Playwright; verification is simpler.
  • A 14B model can learn one coherent set of idioms. Mixing Next.js App Router, React Router framework mode and Vite SPA data fetching produces confused code.

If you need Next.js later, make it a separate adapter and dataset, not more rows in this one.

docs.title: 3.1 Local training target
docs.text:
Model Params Context Local training on 32 GB Role Qwen2.5-Coder-14B-Instruct 14.7B 32K configured, 128K with RoPE scaling Yes, 4-bit QLoRA, 24 of 48 blocks Primary local adapter Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct 7.6B 32K / 128K Yes, all layers, seq 4096 Smoke test, long-context iteration Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct 32.5B 32K / 128K Inference only at 4-bit Occasional judge Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct 30.5B total / 3.3B active 256K native No — inference/teacher only Teacher, judge, bulk generation Qwen3-Coder-Next 80B total / 3B active 256K No API/rented GPU Qwen3-14B 14B 32K Yes General fallback, less code-specialised

Qwen2.5-Coder-14B is the best balance of code quality, React/TS knowledge, Apache-2.0 licensing and local trainability. It has standard attention, no Gated DeltaNet training problem, and a 4-bit MLX conversion.

Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B is a better coder and agent than the 14B, but 30.5B total at 4-bit is ~18–20 GB before activations. Training a 30B MoE with LoRA on 32 GB is not a reliable MLX path. Use it to generate and grade React/Tailwind data, or full fine-tune it on a rented 80 GB GPU.

docs.title: 3.2 The vision limitation
docs.text:
Qwen2.5-Coder is text-only. It cannot consume a screenshot.

That matters because “make it look like this” is a visual task. Two honest options:

  1. Text-spec pipeline (this handbook). A VLM or a human turns the screenshot into a structured design.md: layout, hierarchy, palette, type scale, spacing, components, states, breakpoints, copy. The coder is trained on the spec → code pair. At inference, the user supplies a brief or a VLM-generated spec.
  2. Separate VLM adapter. If you need image → code end-to-end, fine-tune a vision-language model (Qwen3-VL class, or a Design2Code-style model). That is a different dataset, architecture and training run; do not pretend a text coder can see.

The synthetic chapter shows how to use a VLM as a captioner/spec writer, not as the student.

docs.title: 3.3 Memory sketch
docs.text:
Setup Weights Adapter + optimizer Peak estimate Qwen2.5-Coder-7B 4-bit, all 28 blocks, seq 4096 ~4.5 GB ~0.3 GB 12–16 GB Qwen2.5-Coder-14B 4-bit, 24/48 blocks, seq 2048 ~8.7 GB ~0.4 GB 18–23 GB Qwen2.5-Coder-14B 4-bit, 24/48 blocks, seq 3072 ~8.7 GB ~0.4 GB 21–25 GB Qwen2.5-Coder-14B 4-bit, all 48 blocks, seq 2048 ~8.7 GB ~0.8 GB 21–26 GB Qwen2.5-Coder-14B 4-bit, 16/48 blocks, seq 4096 ~8.7 GB ~0.3 GB 21–25 GB

These are estimates. Measure with mlx_lm.lora and mx.get_peak_memory(). Front-end tasks often need more context than a single Java class because they include component code, styles, tests and a design spec; that is why the 7B long-context run exists.

docs.title: 4. What the model must learn
docs.text:
Layer Skills Examples React function components, hooks, ref as prop, Actions, useActionState, useOptimistic, Suspense, use, View Transitions forms, dialogs, lists, optimistic updates TypeScript discriminated unions, generics, satisfies, narrowing, exhaustive checks typed props, API schemas, reducers Tailwind 4 CSS-first theme, tokens, variants, states, responsive, container queries, dark mode buttons, cards, tables, layouts Architecture feature folders, primitives/patterns/pages, composition, server vs client state app shells, design systems, refactors Design hierarchy, spacing, type scale, palette, density, motion, empty/loading/error states dashboards, marketing pages, settings Accessibility semantic HTML, labels, focus, keyboard, contrast, target size, reduced motion forms, menus, dialogs, tables Engineering Vite, Vitest, Testing Library, Playwright, axe, lint, typecheck, build tests, bug fixes, migrations Agent behaviour read before edit, patch format, run checks, screenshot, recover, stop tool trajectories

The model does not need to memorize the whole Tailwind class list. It needs to know the shape of a good component, the token system, and how to verify.

docs.title: 5.1 Feature-based layout
docs.text:
src/
├── app/
│   ├── App.tsx
│   ├── router.tsx
│   ├── providers.tsx
│   └── styles.css
├── components/
│   ├── ui/                 # primitives: Button, Input, Dialog, Card, Badge, Table
│   └── layout/             # AppShell, Sidebar, Topbar, PageHeader
├── features/
│   ├── orders/
│   │   ├── api.ts
│   │   ├── components/
│   │   │   ├── OrderTable.tsx
│   │   │   ├── OrderStatusBadge.tsx
│   │   │   └── EmptyOrders.tsx
│   │   ├── hooks.ts
│   │   ├── schemas.ts
│   │   └── types.ts
│   └── settings/
├── routes/
│   ├── dashboard.tsx
│   ├── orders.tsx
│   └── settings.tsx
├── lib/
│   ├── cn.ts
│   ├── api.ts
│   └── format.ts
└── styles/
    └── theme.css

Rules:

  • components/ui contains presentational primitives with no feature knowledge.
  • features/* owns its API, hooks, schemas, types and components.
  • routes/* composes features into pages; it does not contain business logic.
  • lib is framework-agnostic utilities.
  • Avoid barrel files (index.ts re-exports) in hot paths; they hurt tree-shaking and make diffs noisy. Import directly.
  • One component per file; file name = component name.

docs.title: 5.2 Component taxonomy
docs.text:
Level Examples Rules Primitive Button, Input, Dialog, Tabs, Tooltip headless behaviour + tokens; no domain data Pattern PageHeader, DataTable, EmptyState, ConfirmDialog composable, slot-based; no feature API Feature OrderTable, OrderForm, OrderStatusBadge knows the domain; uses primitives Page OrdersPage routing, data loading, layout; thin

Composition over configuration. A Button with 30 boolean props is a smell; use variants and children/slots.

docs.title: 5.3 State matrix
docs.text:
State Tool Examples Server state TanStack Query lists, details, mutations, cache invalidation URL state React Router useSearchParams filters, pagination, tabs, sort Form state React 19 Actions / useActionState create/edit forms, validation errors Local UI state useState / useReducer open/closed, selected row, draft Global client state Context, or Zustand only if needed theme, session, command palette Derived state compute during render filtered lists, counts

Rules:

  • Do not copy server data into useState; it creates stale duplicates.
  • Do not put filters in local state when they should survive reload; use the URL.
  • Do not use useEffect to derive state from props; compute it.
  • Do not use useEffect to fetch when TanStack Query or a route loader is available.
  • Keep global state small. A 14B model will overuse Context if the data shows it.

docs.title: 5.4 Server state with TanStack Query
docs.text:
import { useQuery } from "@tanstack/react-query";
import { ordersQuery } from "@/features/orders/api";

export function OrdersPage() {
  const { data, isPending, isError, refetch } = useQuery(ordersQuery.list());
  if (isPending) return <OrdersSkeleton />;
  if (isError) return <ErrorState onRetry={refetch} />;
  if (data.length === 0) return <EmptyOrders />;
  return <OrderTable orders={data} />;
}

The component has four explicit states: loading, error, empty, content. Training data must show all four; a model trained only on the happy path will ship blank screens.

docs.title: 5.5 React 19 patterns
docs.text:
ref as a prop — no forwardRef wrapper:

export function Field({ ref, ...props }: FieldProps) {
  return <input ref={ref} {...props} />;
}

Actions and useActionState:

const [state, action, pending] = useActionState(updateProfile, initialState);

return (
  <form action={action}>
    <Field name="name" defaultValue={state.values?.name} />
    {state.errors?.name && <FieldError>{state.errors.name}</FieldError>}
    <Button type="submit" disabled={pending}>Save</Button>
  </form>
);

useOptimistic for instant feedback, with rollback on error.

use for reading a promise or context in a client component, inside Suspense.

View Transitions for route/list transitions; always respect prefers-reduced-motion.

React Compiler is stable (1.0, Oct 2025). If it is enabled, do not sprinkle useMemo/useCallback everywhere; write plain components and let the compiler memoize. Do not break the Rules of React.

docs.title: 5.6 Routing
docs.text:
React Router 8 data mode:

import { createBrowserRouter } from "react-router";
import { RouterProvider } from "react-router/dom";

const router = createBrowserRouter([
  { path: "/", element: <AppShell />, children: [
    { index: true, element: <DashboardPage /> },
    { path: "orders", element: <OrdersPage /> },
    { path: "orders/:id", element: <OrderDetailPage /> },
  ]},
]);

export function App() {
  return <RouterProvider router={router} />;
}

Use errorElement / ErrorBoundary for route errors; use lazy for route code splitting.

docs.title: 6.1 Tokens, not raw palette
docs.text:
@import "tailwindcss";

@custom-variant dark (&:where(.dark, .dark *));

@theme {
  --font-sans: "Inter Variable", ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif;
  --font-mono: "JetBrains Mono", ui-monospace, monospace;

  --color-canvas: oklch(0.985 0.003 250);
  --color-surface: oklch(1 0 0);
  --color-ink: oklch(0.22 0.02 260);
  --color-muted: oklch(0.55 0.02 260);
  --color-border: oklch(0.91 0.01 260);
  --color-brand: oklch(0.58 0.19 275);
  --color-brand-foreground: oklch(0.99 0 0);
  --color-success: oklch(0.52 0.12 155);
  --color-danger: oklch(0.55 0.18 27);

  --radius-card: 1rem;
  --shadow-card: 0 1px 2px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.04), 0 8px 24px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.06);
}

@layer base {
  html { color-scheme: light; }
  .dark { color-scheme: dark; }
  body { @apply bg-canvas text-ink antialiased; }
}

.dark {
  --color-canvas: oklch(0.16 0.01 260);
  --color-surface: oklch(0.20 0.012 260);
  --color-ink: oklch(0.96 0.004 260);
  --color-muted: oklch(0.72 0.015 260);
  --color-border: oklch(0.30 0.015 260);
  --color-success: oklch(0.72 0.12 155);
  --color-danger: oklch(0.70 0.16 27);
}

Then components use semantic classes:

<section className="rounded-card border border-border bg-surface p-6 shadow-card">
  <h2 className="text-lg font-semibold tracking-tight">Recent orders</h2>
  <p className="mt-1 text-sm text-muted">Updated five minutes ago.</p>
</section>

Not:

<section className="rounded-2xl border border-gray-200 bg-white p-6 shadow-lg">

The second is not “wrong”; it is unmaintainable and it will not survive dark mode or a rebrand.

docs.title: 6.2 Variants with CVA and cn
docs.text:
// src/lib/cn.ts
import { clsx, type ClassValue } from "clsx";
import { twMerge } from "tailwind-merge";

export function cn(...inputs: ClassValue[]) {
  return twMerge(clsx(inputs));
}

// src/components/ui/button.tsx
import { cva, type VariantProps } from "class-variance-authority";
import type { ComponentProps } from "react";
import { cn } from "@/lib/cn";

const button = cva(
  "inline-flex items-center justify-center gap-2 rounded-lg font-medium transition-colors " +
    "focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-brand " +
    "disabled:pointer-events-none disabled:opacity-50 motion-reduce:transition-none",
  {
    variants: {
      variant: {
        primary: "bg-brand text-brand-foreground hover:bg-brand/90",
        secondary: "border border-border bg-surface text-ink hover:bg-canvas",
        ghost: "text-ink hover:bg-canvas",
        danger: "bg-red-600 text-white hover:bg-red-700",
      },
      size: {
        sm: "h-9 px-3 text-sm",
        md: "h-10 px-4 text-sm",
        lg: "h-11 px-5 text-base",
      },
    },
    defaultVariants: { variant: "primary", size: "md" },
  },
);

type ButtonProps = ComponentProps<"button"> & VariantProps<typeof button>;

export function Button({ className, variant, size, type = "button", ...props }: ButtonProps) {
  return <button type={type} className={cn(button({ variant, size }), className)} {...props} />;
}

Why this shape:

  • variants are typed and exhaustive;
  • cn resolves conflicting Tailwind classes;
  • type="button" is the default, preventing accidental form submits;
  • focus styles are explicit;
  • motion respects reduced motion;
  • no raw hex in the component.

docs.title: 6.3 Rules that prevent broken Tailwind
docs.text:
• No dynamic class construction: bg-${color}-500 is invisible to Tailwind's scanner. Use a map of complete class strings.
  • No arbitrary hex (bg-[#6d28d9]) when a token exists.
  • No @apply in component CSS without @reference in v4 CSS modules.
  • No tailwind.config.js for a new v4 project; use @theme. Legacy config is only via @config.
  • No @tailwind base; use @import "tailwindcss".
  • No outline-none on focusable elements; use outline-hidden for the old behaviour or an explicit focus ring.
  • No bg-opacity-*; use bg-black/50.
  • Use gap-* instead of space-x-*/space-y-* in new flex/grid layouts.
  • Use min-h-dvh, not min-h-screen, for mobile browser chrome.
  • Use text-balance for headings, text-pretty for body copy.
  • Use container queries (@container, @container-size) for reusable components, viewport breakpoints for page layout.

docs.title: 6.4 Dark mode
docs.text:
Class strategy:

@custom-variant dark (&:where(.dark, .dark *));

Toggle document.documentElement.classList.toggle("dark"); persist the choice; respect prefers-color-scheme on first load. Do not hardcode dark: colors that ignore the token system. Test contrast in both themes.

docs.title: 6.5 Responsive and fluid
docs.text:
• Mobile-first; test 320, 375, 768, 1024, 1440.
  • Page container: mx-auto w-full max-w-7xl px-4 sm:px-6 lg:px-8.
  • Fluid type only where it helps: text-[clamp(1.75rem,1.2rem+2vw,2.75rem)].
  • Tables: wrap in overflow-x-auto, keep a caption and scope="col".
  • Never hide critical actions at small widths; move them into a menu, not into oblivion.
  • Check for horizontal overflow at 320px.

docs.title: 7. Accessibility: WCAG 2.2 AA as a gate
docs.text:
Requirement Practical rule Semantic HTML button for actions, a for navigation, nav/main/header/footer, one h1 Labels every input has a visible <label> or aria-label; placeholder is not a label Keyboard every action reachable by Tab; Enter/Space activate; Escape closes overlays Focus visible focus ring; not obscured by sticky headers (2.4.11); scroll-padding-top Target size at least 24×24 CSS px (2.5.8 AA); 44×44 is a good default Contrast 4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large text and UI boundaries Images meaningful alt; decorative alt=""; no text baked into images Forms error text linked with aria-describedby; aria-invalid; summary at top Motion motion-reduce: / prefers-reduced-motion; no autoplay Dragging provide a non-drag alternative (2.5.7) Auth no cognitive-function test; paste and password managers allowed

Use Radix primitives for dialogs, menus, tabs, tooltips, switches and selects; they handle focus trapping, roving tabindex, typeahead, escape and ARIA. Then style with Tailwind.

axe catches maybe 30–50% of issues. Manual keyboard and screen-reader checks remain mandatory.

docs.title: 8.1 Performance
docs.text:
• Route-level code splitting with lazy and Suspense.
  • Image dimensions, srcset, loading="lazy" below the fold, fetchpriority="high" for LCP.
  • Fonts: font-display: swap, preload only the used weight, subset.
  • Avoid layout shift: reserve space for async content, skeletons with the same dimensions.
  • INP: keep event handlers small; avoid long lists without virtualization; use startTransition for non-urgent updates.
  • React Compiler can remove unnecessary memoization; measure before adding useMemo.
  • Bundle analysis: vite build --mode analyze or rollup-plugin-visualizer; budget per route.
  • CSS: Tailwind emits only used classes; avoid huge @apply layers.

docs.title: 8.2 Visual quality rubric
docs.text:
“Nice” is not a class list. Grade each screen 1–5 on:

  1. Hierarchy — one primary action per view; scanning order is obvious.
  2. Spacing — consistent 4/8px rhythm; generous whitespace; aligned edges.
  3. Typography — one display face, one body face; 1.2–1.333 scale; 45–75 characters per line.
  4. Color — one accent, neutral canvas, semantic states; contrast holds in dark mode.
  5. Density — tables and forms are scannable; not cramped, not airy to the point of emptiness.
  6. States — loading, empty, error, disabled, hover, focus, active, selected.
  7. Responsiveness — no overflow; navigation adapts; touch targets hold.
  8. Restraint — motion and decoration serve meaning; no generic “AI” gradient soup.

docs.title: 8.3 “AI slop” to reject in training data
docs.text:
• purple-to-pink gradient on every hero;
  • glassmorphism cards with no hierarchy;
  • 32px radius on everything;
  • emoji as the icon system;
  • Lorem ipsum, fake testimonials, fake logos;
  • low-contrast gray text on white;
  • centered everything, no grid;
  • five different shadows and radii;
  • decorative animation that ignores reduced motion;
  • a dashboard with only a happy path.

Train the opposite: real copy, one accent, a tokenized palette, consistent radii, subtle elevation, a clear grid, and explicit states.

docs.title: 9. Testing strategy
docs.text:
Layer Tool What to verify Type tsc --noEmit (TS 7) no type errors, no removed options Lint ESLint 10 + react-hooks + jsx-a11y hooks rules, a11y, imports Unit/component Vitest 5 + Testing Library behavior via roles, not implementation Stories Storybook 10.6 (optional) variants, states, a11y addon E2E Playwright 1.64 critical flows, responsive, screenshots A11y @axe-core/playwright serious/critical violations = 0 Visual Playwright toHaveScreenshot refactors preserve appearance Build vite build production build, no missing imports

Type-check and build are separate: Vite transpiles without type-checking. An agent that only runs vite build can ship type errors.

docs.title: 10. What not to mix
docs.text: Mix Symptom Rule React 18 + 19 idioms forwardRef everywhere, ReactDOM.render, useFormState tag react: 19 Tailwind 3 + 4 @tailwind base + @theme, wrong shadow/radius scale tag tailwind: 4 Next.js + Vite SPA next/link, "use server", route handlers in a Vite app separate track React Router 7 + 8 react-router-dom imports tag router: 8 TypeScript 6 + 7 config baseUrl, moduleResolution: node TS 7-compatible tsconfig CSS-in-JS + Tailwind two styling systems, specificity fights pick one Redux + TanStack Query duplicated server state Query for server, Context/Zustand for UI

docs.title: 11. The data plan in one table
docs.text:
Bucket Share Source Components/primitives 20% shadcn/ui, Radix, synthetic Pages/layouts 15% synthetic, react-code-instructions Data/forms 15% TanStack Query docs, synthetic Design system/refactor 10% synthetic + tokens Accessibility 10% synthetic + axe Testing 10% synthetic + Playwright + Testing Library Bug fix/recovery 10% commits, synthetic Migration (React 18→19, Tailwind 3→4, Router 7→8, TS 6→7) 5% synthetic Negative/refusal/security 5% synthetic

Details, licenses and exact dataset IDs are in 23 — React & Tailwind datasets. The training runbook is 24 — React fine-tuning. The synthetic pipeline is 25 — React synthetic data.

docs.title: 23 — React & Tailwind datasets: what exists, what is missing, and how to mix it
docs.text:
Last verified: 25 October 2026. Dataset sizes and licenses were checked against the Hugging Face API and dataset cards; re-check before a large download.

There is no single “React 19 + Tailwind 4 + good design system” dataset. What exists falls into six families:

  1. Raw code corpora — The Stack v3, filtered to JS/TS/TSX.
  2. Code instruction data — OpenCodeInstruct, Magicoder, React-specific instruction sets.
  3. Complete React apps — react-code-instructions.
  4. Design-to-code / visual data — WebSight v0.2 (HTML + Tailwind), Design2Code.
  5. Agentic front-end benchmarks — Webdev-Bench, SWE-bench Multilingual, Multi-SWE-bench, SWE-bench Multimodal.
  6. Repository sources — shadcn/ui, Tailwind, React, Radix, TanStack, Storybook, Playwright.

The missing pieces — Tailwind 4 tokens, design-system refactors, accessibility, visual quality, testing — are exactly what synthetic generation and execution verification are for. See 25 — React synthetic data.

docs.title: 1. Inventory
docs.text:

filter React/TS ise-uiuc/Magicoder-OSS-Instruct-75K OSS-Instruct synthetic code instructions 75K MIT (GPT-3.5 output; OpenAI policy) diversity; filter JS/TS ise-uiuc/Magicoder-Evol-Instruct-110K Evol-Instruct complexity 110K Apache-2.0 harder tasks; filter JS/TS cfahlgren1/react-code-instructions Complete React apps generated by Llama 3.1 / DeepSeek 74,428 rows / ~907 MB MIT complete-app style; quality varies HuggingFaceM4/WebSight (v0.2) Synthetic websites: screenshot + HTML + Tailwind 1,922,671 rows / ~285 GB CC-BY-4.0 layout/Tailwind vocabulary; license check SWE-bench/SWE-bench_Multimodal JS/TS issues with screenshots/mockups 480 test + 100 dev no license tag; source repos visual issue eval only code_search_net JS functions with docstrings 1,857,835 JS functions; Avoid for a release: Devendra174/react-code-dataset (no license), summykai/tailwind-v4-sft-mix-001 (no license), lazos/frontend-agent-sft (other). They may be useful for experiments; do not redistribute an adapter trained on them without a license audit.

docs.title: 2. Raw code: The Stack v3
docs.text:
The Stack v3 is the current large open code corpus:

  • 15.9 TB training subset, ~3.6T tokens, 713 languages, 173M repositories.
  • Full corpus: 113.7 TB, 770 languages, 224M repositories.
  • ODC-BY; per-file license metadata; gated full corpus.
  • Inline file contents and language, license_type, detected_licenses.

For React/Tailwind:

  1. Filter language to TypeScript/JavaScript/TSX/JSX.
  2. Prefer repositories with package.json, react, tailwindcss, vite.
  3. Keep permissive license_type/detected_licenses; drop unknown for a release.
  4. Sample repositories, not random files, so you get imports, components and tests together.
  5. Do not train on raw files for SFT. Use them as seed repos for synthetic tasks.

A 50k–200k file sample is plenty for a LoRA; a 3T-token continued-pretraining run is a different project and belongs on rented GPUs.

docs.title: 3.1 OpenCodeInstruct
docs.text:
• 5M instruction/answer pairs, ~19 GB, CC-BY-4.0.
  • Fields include input, output, domain, generation_algorithm, unit_tests, tests_execution_status, average_test_score.
  • Best large public starting point for code SFT, but Python-heavy and multilingual.
  • Filter to React/TS by checking for import React, tsx, useState, tailwind, className=.
  • Prefer rows with passing tests; do not assume the metadata is correct.
  • It is not a React design-system dataset; it teaches general code instruction following.

docs.title: 3.2 Magicoder
docs.text:
• OSS-Instruct-75K: MIT; generated by GPT-3.5, so OpenAI's usage policy applies.
  • Evol-Instruct-110K: Apache-2.0.
  • Good for diversity and harder reasoning; weak for React 19, Tailwind 4 and repo context.
  • Filter JS/TS; drop LeetCode-style puzzles if you want production front-end style.

docs.title: 3.3 react-code-instructions
docs.text:
• 74,428 rows, ~907 MB, MIT.
  • Complete React apps (Artifact-style) generated by Llama 3.1 70B/405B and DeepSeek Chat V3.
  • Useful for whole-app shape: routing, pages, components, mock data, styling.
  • Caveats:
  • generated by 2024-era models, likely React 18 / Tailwind 3;
  • quality varies; some apps are toy clones;
  • no tests or build verification;
  • possible brand/trademark imitation (LinkedIn clone, Apple Store clone).
  • Use it as a style/structure seed, not as gold. Rebuild, typecheck, test and retag to React 19/Tailwind 4.

docs.title: 3.4 CodeSearchNet (JS)
docs.text:
• 1,857,835 JavaScript functions; 157,988 with documentation.
  • Good for docstring→function, summarization, code search.
  • Not React, not components, not Tailwind.
  • Optional; low priority for a UI adapter.

docs.title: 4.1 WebSight v0.2
docs.text:
This is the most relevant public visual corpus for Tailwind:

  • 1,922,671 synthetic websites; screenshot + HTML + Tailwind CSS.
  • ~285 GB; CC-BY-4.0.
  • Generated from LLM website ideas, then code; real images in v0.2.
  • llm_generated_idea gives a text description you can reuse as a brief.
  • The Tailwind is from the v3 era (2024). It is not a Tailwind 4 corpus.

How to use it:

  1. Sample 10k–50k rows; do not download 285 GB for a LoRA.
  2. Use llm_generated_idea as a design brief; use the HTML/Tailwind as a layout/class reference.
  3. Convert selected examples to React components (dangerouslySetInnerHTML → JSX) with a verified synthetic pass.
  4. Add a Tailwind 3 → 4 migration task for a subset; that teaches the renames and CSS-first config.
  5. Use screenshots for a VLM captioner, not as direct input to Qwen2.5-Coder.

docs.title: 4.2 Design2Code
docs.text:
• 484 real webpages from C4 validation; screenshot + HTML; images replaced with placeholders.
  • ODC-BY; evaluation only.
  • Metrics: rendered visual similarity (CLIP), element matching (position/text/color), block match.
  • Good for measuring visual fidelity of a design-to-code system.
  • Qwen2.5-Coder is text-only, so it cannot be evaluated on the screenshot input directly. Use a VLM front-end or convert the screenshot to a written spec first.

docs.title: 4.3 The text-only rule
docs.text:
Do not put screenshots in a Qwen2.5-Coder training row. The model cannot see them, and the template will not encode them. Options:

  • VLM caption → design spec → coder (recommended; this handbook).
  • Separate VLM adapter (Qwen3-VL class) for image → code.
  • Human-written brief for the highest-quality examples.

A text coder trained on “design.md → code” can still produce beautiful UIs; it just needs the design expressed in words and tokens.

docs.title: 5.1 Webdev-Bench
docs.text:
• 40 composite front-end tasks over an evolving Vite + React project.
  • 188 milestones, 1,125 checklist items; functional, visual, interaction, coverage and data dimensions.
  • Seed types: PRD (20), brownfield (11), replicate (9).
  • MIT; evaluation only.
  • This is the closest public benchmark to “keep modifying a real front-end and keep it working”. It is also a good template for your own golden set: milestones + observable checklist, not a single prompt.

docs.title: 5.2 SWE-bench Multilingual
docs.text:
• 300 issue-resolution tasks; JavaScript 26, TypeScript 17.
  • Repos include preactjs/preact, vuejs/core, facebook/docusaurus, babel/babel, axios/axios, mrdoob/three.js.
  • MIT; evaluation only.
  • Good for repo-level JS/TS reasoning, but not specifically React UI or Tailwind.

docs.title: 5.3 Multi-SWE-bench
docs.text:
• 1,632 tasks; TypeScript 224, JavaScript 356.
  • other license; source repositories have their own licenses.
  • Evaluation only; do not train on the benchmark.
  • Useful for measuring multi-file edits and test-driven repair.

docs.title: 5.4 SWE-bench Multimodal
docs.text:
• 480 test + 100 dev tasks from 17 JavaScript/TypeScript repositories; issues include screenshots, mockups or diagrams.
  • No license tag on the dataset; the source repos have licenses. Treat as evaluation only.
  • This is the right benchmark if your system accepts images; not for a text-only Qwen2.5-Coder.

docs.title: 5.5 What these teach
docs.text:
• Read a file tree and find the relevant component.
  • Change multiple files without breaking imports.
  • Run the test/build command and recover.
  • Preserve behavior while refactoring.
  • Produce a patch, not a lecture.

Single-file instruction data does not teach these. Mix repository tasks with component tasks.

docs.title: 6. Repository sources: the best “design system” data
docs.text: There is no public “good taste” dataset. The best seed is real, permissively licensed code:

docs.title: 6.1 shadcn/ui
docs.text:
• MIT; copy-paste components built on Radix + Tailwind.
  • Excellent patterns for:
  • cn and CVA variants;
  • data-slot, data-state, aria-* styling;
  • dialogs, dropdowns, tabs, tooltips, forms;
  • dark mode tokens.
  • Do not copy the whole library into every example; extract the pattern and generate a small component.

docs.title: 6.2 Radix Primitives
docs.text:
• MIT; accessible headless components.
  • Use for focus management, keyboard interaction, ARIA, portal/overlay behaviour.
  • Training data should show composition (Dialog.Root, Dialog.Trigger, Dialog.Content) rather than reimplementing focus traps.

docs.title: 6.3 Tailwind CSS repo
docs.text:
• MIT; tests and examples for v4 features.
  • Good for edge cases: @theme, @utility, @variant, container queries, @starting-style, scrollbars.
  • Do not train on the framework's internal source as if it were app code.

docs.title: 6.4 React repo
docs.text:
• MIT; tests, fixtures, docs.
  • Good for React 19 behaviours: useActionState, useOptimistic, use, ref cleanup, View Transitions.
  • Not a UI dataset.

docs.title: 6.5 TanStack Query
docs.text:
• MIT; examples for queries, mutations, optimistic updates, invalidation, Suspense.
  • Extract patterns, not the library internals.

docs.title: 6.6 Storybook and Playwright
docs.text:
• MIT / Apache-2.0.
  • Storybook: stories, states, a11y addon, interaction tests.
  • Playwright: E2E, visual snapshots, accessibility scans.
  • These are verification sources; the training rows are the verified tasks.

docs.title: 7. The gap: Tailwind 4, design systems, accessibility
docs.text:
No public dataset reliably labels:

  • “this component uses semantic tokens instead of raw palette”;
  • “this layout has good hierarchy and spacing”;
  • “this refactor improves composition without changing behaviour”;
  • “this interaction is keyboard-accessible”;
  • “this is a Tailwind 4 migration, not a v3 example”.

The honest approach:

  1. Mine real components from MIT repositories.
  2. Generate tasks from a working baseline: add a variant, extract a primitive, tokenize colors, add a dark theme, fix a focus trap.
  3. Verify with the compiler, tests, Playwright and axe.
  4. Grade visual quality with a rubric and a human/VLM pairwise review.
  5. Keep a human-labeled slice to calibrate the rubric.

A component that builds, passes tests, has zero serious axe violations and looks good at 320/768/1440 is a much stronger example than a prose “make it beautiful”.

docs.title: 8. The mix
docs.text:
For a first React/Tailwind adapter, aim for 2–4M tokens (roughly 2,000–5,000 examples after truncation):

Bucket Share Source Why Components/primitives 20% shadcn/ui, Radix, synthetic teaches the component shape Pages/layouts 15% synthetic, react-code-instructions teaches composition and hierarchy Data/forms 15% TanStack Query, React 19 Actions, synthetic teaches states and validation Design system/refactor 10% synthetic + tokens teaches consistency Accessibility 10% synthetic + axe teaches keyboard/focus/semantics Testing 10% synthetic + Playwright/RTL teaches verification Bug fix/recovery 10% commits, synthetic teaches multi-file reasoning Migration 5% synthetic React 18→19, Tailwind 3→4, Router 7→8, TS 6→7 Negative/refusal/security 5% synthetic teaches boundaries

A mature adapter can grow to 8–12M tokens. Scale task families, not paraphrases.

docs.title: 9. Quality filters
docs.text:
Run these before tokenization:

  • Type-check: tsc --noEmit with a TypeScript 7-compatible tsconfig.
  • Lint: ESLint 10 (TypeScript 6 API bridge), react-hooks, jsx-a11y.
  • Unit: Vitest 5 + Testing Library; tests assert behaviour via roles.
  • E2E: Playwright; critical flows pass.
  • Build: vite build; no missing imports or unresolved aliases.
  • A11y: axe serious/critical = 0.
  • Responsive: no horizontal overflow at 320, 768, 1440.
  • Tailwind 4: no @tailwind base, no bg-opacity-*, no flex-shrink-*, no dynamic class names, no outline-none on focus.
  • React 19: no ReactDOM.render, no useFormState; forwardRef/React.FC are warnings, not errors.
  • No raw hex when a token exists; inline style={{ color: ... }} is a warning.
  • No unsanitized dangerouslySetInnerHTML; no secrets; no VITE_* secrets.
  • No any/@ts-ignore/console.log/TODO in final answers.
  • License metadata present; reject unknown/non-commercial for a release.
  • Dedup exact and near-duplicate components/pages; split by repo/commit.

scripts/validate_react_dataset.py automates the static checks. It is not a browser, compiler or test runner.

docs.title: 10. Contamination and evaluation hygiene
docs.text:
• Hold out Webdev-Bench, Design2Code, SWE-bench Multilingual (JS/TS), Multi-SWE-bench (TS/JS) and SWE-bench Multimodal.
  • Run 13-gram overlap between training rows and every benchmark.
  • Split by repository and base commit, not random row.
  • Hold out entire shadcn/ui component families, Tailwind versions or React releases for a time-based test.
  • Keep a private golden set of 100–200 tasks from your own product.
  • Report the base model and adapter on the same prompt, viewport, seed and browser.
  • For visual tasks, use pairwise human/VLM comparison, not an absolute “beauty score”.

A model that memorizes shadcn/ui examples will look great on a shadcn clone and fail on your design system. The private golden set is the cure.

docs.title: 11. Canonical rows
docs.text:
A component task:

{
  "messages": [
    {"role": "system", "content": "You are a senior React/TypeScript/Tailwind engineer. Target React 19.3, TypeScript 7-compatible source, Vite 8 and Tailwind 4.3. Use semantic tokens, accessible primitives, and run typecheck/lint/test/build before claiming success."},
    {"role": "user", "content": "Build a `StatCard` component for a dashboard. Props: label, value, delta (optional, signed number), icon (optional Lucide component). Show a positive/negative delta with an arrow and an accessible label. Use design tokens, not raw colors. Include loading and empty states. Add a Vitest test."},
    {"role": "assistant", "content": "```tsx
import type { LucideIcon } from "lucide-react";
import { ArrowDownRight, ArrowUpRight } from "lucide-react";
import { cn } from "@/lib/cn";

type StatCardProps = {
  label: string;
  value: string;
  delta?: number;
  icon?: LucideIcon;
  loading?: boolean;
};

export function StatCard({ label, value, delta, icon: Icon, loading }: StatCardProps) {
  const positive = typeof delta === "number" && delta >= 0;
  const DeltaIcon = positive ? ArrowUpRight : ArrowDownRight;

  return (
    <section className="rounded-card border border-border bg-surface p-5 shadow-card">
      <div className="flex items-start justify-between gap-4">
        <div>
          <p className="text-sm text-muted">{label}</p>
          {loading ? (
            <div className="mt-2 h-8 w-24 animate-pulse rounded-md bg-canvas" aria-hidden="true" />
          ) : (
            <p className="mt-1 text-2xl font-semibold tracking-tight">{value}</p>
          )}
        </div>
        {Icon ? <Icon className="size-5 text-muted" aria-hidden="true" /> : null}
      </div>
      {typeof delta === "number" && !loading ? (
        <p className={cn("mt-3 inline-flex items-center gap-1 text-sm", positive ? "text-emerald-700 dark:text-emerald-400" : "text-red-700 dark:text-red-400")}>
          <DeltaIcon className="size-4" aria-hidden="true" />
          <span>{Math.abs(delta)}%</span>
          <span className="text-muted">vs last month</span>
        </p>
      ) : null}
    </section>
  );
}
```"}
  ],
  "meta": {
    "repo": "design-system-example",
    "license": "MIT",
    "category": "component",
    "versions": {"react": "19.3", "tailwind": "4.3", "vite": "8", "ts": "7.0"},
    "test_command": "npm run typecheck && npm test -- --run && npm run build"
  }
}

A page task with tools: see data/examples/react-train.example.jsonl. For Qwen2.5-Coder, tool arguments must be objects:

{"name": "read_file", "arguments": {"path": "src/features/orders/components/OrderTable.tsx"}}

Use prepare_dataset.py --arguments-format dict.

docs.title: 12. Sources
docs.text:

docs.title: 24 — Fine-tuning a Qwen coder for React and Tailwind
docs.text:
Last verified: 25 October 2026 against mlx-lm 0.32.2 and the Qwen2.5-Coder tokenizer template. The commands were not executed on the target Mac in this environment.

This is the runbook for the front-end track. It assumes:

  • macOS Apple Silicon with MLX installed (03-macos-setup.md);
  • Node 24 LTS and npm for building/evaluating the React projects;
  • React/Tailwind data in data/react/processed/{train,valid,test}.jsonl (23-react-datasets.md);
  • 32 GB unified memory.

The default is Qwen2.5-Coder-14B-Instruct 4-bit QLoRA, adapting 24 of 48 blocks at 3,072 tokens. The 7B all-layer run is the smoke test and the long-context fallback.

docs.title: 0. The recipe in one table
docs.text:
Choice Value Why Base mlx-community/Qwen2.5-Coder-14B-Instruct-4bit code-specialised, Apache-2.0, fits 32 GB Method 4-bit QLoRA, lora base frozen; adapter small Blocks 24 of 48 memory-safe for 3K context Rank / scale 16 / 2.0 PEFT alpha=32 equivalent LR 1e-4 standard LoRA range with scale=2 Effective batch 8 (1 × 8 accumulation) LoRA prefers 8–16 Sequence 3072 component + styles + tests Iterations 300 ~4–5M tokens; adjust to your data Masking mask_prompt: true train only the final assistant turn Checkpoint every 50 short run; keep options

Front-end tasks are longer than single-function tasks. At 12–18 tok/s, 300 iterations × 8 × ~1,800 tokens (~4.3M) is roughly 65–100 hours. For a two-day run, use 200 iterations or a 1.5M-token dataset. Do not guess; measure with token_stats.py.

docs.title: 1. Preflight
docs.text:
cd ~/work/qwen-kali-agent
source .venv/bin/activate

node -v            # expect 24.x LTS
npm -v
npx playwright --version

python scripts/check_env.py

Checklist:

  • Node 24 LTS; not Node 26 Current.
  • npm ci passes on the reference React project.
  • npm run typecheck passes.
  • npm run lint passes.
  • npm run build passes.
  • npx playwright test passes (Chromium installed).
  • MLX sees the GPU (mx.device_info()).
  • 100+ GB free disk.
  • The React data exists and is non-empty.
  • No secrets in data/react/.
  • You have a baseline evaluation of the base model.

Node is only for data generation and evaluation. MLX training does not need Node, but you cannot verify React data without it.

docs.title: 2.1 Mine seeds from a permissive repository
docs.text:
mkdir -p data/react/{raw,interim,processed,processed-long,golden}

python scripts/mine_react_commits.py \
  --repo ~/src/shadcn-ui/ui \
  --out data/react/interim/shadcn-commits.jsonl \
  --limit 300 --only-with-tests --license MIT

Each row has a base commit, task text, changed files, gold patch, package manager and test command. It is a seed, not a finished training row. Use 25 — React synthetic data to turn it into a verified task and a new solution.

docs.title: 2.2 Normalize and split
docs.text:
Qwen2.5-Coder requires tool arguments as objects:

python scripts/prepare_dataset.py \
  data/react/interim/all.jsonl \
  --out data/react/processed \
  --arguments-format dict \
  --split 0.9 0.05 0.05

For the 4K run, build a separate split from rows whose rendered length is between 2,049 and 4,096 tokens. Inspect the distribution with token_stats.py, then filter before prepare_dataset.py; do not include 8K examples in a 4K run. If a row is longer than 4,096, split the trajectory or drop it rather than truncating a tool call.

docs.title: 2.3 Validate
docs.text:
python scripts/validate_dataset.py data/react/processed/train.jsonl \
  --tools examples/react/tools.json

python scripts/validate_react_dataset.py data/react/processed/train.jsonl \
  --tools examples/react/tools.json --require-dict-arguments --strict

The React validator catches:

  • legacy Tailwind v3 directives and v4-removed utilities;
  • ReactDOM.render, useFormState, class components, React.FC;
  • dynamic class construction;
  • unsanitized dangerouslySetInnerHTML;
  • missing alt, button type, rel on _blank;
  • div click handlers without roles;
  • any, @ts-ignore, console.log, TODO;
  • probable secrets;
  • tool arguments stored as strings instead of objects.

It is a linter, not a compiler or a browser. The real filter is tsc, ESLint, Vitest, Vite, Playwright and axe.

docs.title: 2.4 Measure tokens
docs.text:
python scripts/token_stats.py data/react/processed/train.jsonl \
  --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-14B-Instruct

Choose max_seq_length at the 99th percentile, rounded to 256. If p99 is 3,400, use 3,072 and split long rows; do not default to 4,096 because a few examples are long.

docs.title: 2.5 A useful dataset size
docs.text:
• First adapter: 2–3M tokens, 2,000–5,000 examples.
  • Mature adapter: 5–10M tokens, 8k+ examples.
  • Do not dump 100k raw components; the model learns style from a few thousand verified tasks.

Mix from 23-react-datasets.md §8: 20% components, 15% pages, 15% data/forms, 10% design system, 10% a11y, 10% testing, 10% bug fix, 5% migration, 5% refusal.

docs.title: 3.1 7B smoke / long context — configs/qwen2.5-coder-7b-react.yaml
docs.text:
model: mlx-community/Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct-4bit
train: true
data: data/react/processed
fine_tune_type: lora
optimizer: adamw
num_layers: -1
batch_size: 1
iters: 300
val_batches: 25
learning_rate: 1.5e-4
steps_per_report: 10
steps_per_eval: 100
save_every: 100
max_seq_length: 4096
grad_checkpoint: true
grad_accumulation_steps: 8
mask_prompt: true
adapter_path: adapters/qwen25-coder-7b-react
seed: 42
lora_parameters:
  rank: 16
  dropout: 0.05
  scale: 2.0
lr_schedule:
  name: cosine_decay
  warmup: 30
  arguments: [1.5e-4, 300, 1.0e-6]
optimizer_config:
  adamw:
    weight_decay: 0.01

All 28 blocks fit comfortably. Use it to validate the data/template and to handle 4K multi-file examples quickly.

docs.title: 3.2 14B default — configs/qwen2.5-coder-14b-react.yaml
docs.text:
model: mlx-community/Qwen2.5-Coder-14B-Instruct-4bit
train: true
data: data/react/processed
fine_tune_type: lora
optimizer: adamw
num_layers: 24
batch_size: 1
iters: 300
val_batches: 25
learning_rate: 1.0e-4
steps_per_report: 10
steps_per_eval: 100
save_every: 50
max_seq_length: 3072
grad_checkpoint: true
grad_accumulation_steps: 8
mask_prompt: true
adapter_path: adapters/qwen25-coder-14b-react
seed: 42
lora_parameters:
  rank: 16
  dropout: 0.05
  scale: 2.0
lr_schedule:
  name: cosine_decay
  warmup: 30
  arguments: [1.0e-4, 300, 1.0e-6]
optimizer_config:
  adamw:
    weight_decay: 0.01

Peak is the risk: 21–25 GB at 3,072. If it OOMs, reduce sequence to 2,048 first; then blocks to 16.

docs.title: 3.3 14B all layers — configs/qwen2.5-coder-14b-react-all-layers.yaml
docs.text: All 48 blocks, seq 2,048, LR 8e-5, 250 iterations. Higher capacity, higher activation memory. Run after the 24-layer adapter is evaluated; drop to 32 blocks if it OOMs.

docs.title: 3.4 14B long context — configs/qwen2.5-coder-14b-react-longctx.yaml
docs.text: Last 16 blocks, seq 4,096, LR 8e-5, 250 iterations. For page + component + tests examples that exceed 3K. 4K roughly doubles activation memory versus 2K; fewer blocks compensate.

docs.title: 3.5 How many iterations?
docs.text:
tokens_seen ≈ iters × batch_size × grad_accumulation_steps × avg_tokens_per_sample
iters ≈ epochs × dataset_tokens / (batch_size × grad_accumulation_steps × avg_tokens_per_sample)

Example: 2.5M-token dataset, average 1,800 tokens, effective batch 8, 1 epoch:

iters = 1 × 2,500,000 / (8 × 1,800) ≈ 174

So 175–200 iterations is one epoch; 300 is ~1.5–1.7 epochs. Use validation loss and the golden set; do not train to a fixed number.

docs.title: 4. Verify what the adapter actually covers
docs.text:
Before spending hours:

python scripts/check_lora.py \
  --model mlx-community/Qwen2.5-Coder-14B-Instruct-4bit \
  --num-layers 24 --rank 16 --scale 2

Expected:

  • 24 adapted blocks of 48;
  • 7 projections per block (q_proj, k_proj, v_proj, o_proj, gate_proj, up_proj, down_proj);
  • ~168 LoRA modules;
  • roughly 34M trainable parameters.

All-layer 14B: ~336 modules, ~69M trainable parameters. 7B all 28 blocks: ~196 modules, roughly 40M trainable parameters.

Exact numbers depend on the MLX version and embedding handling. If you see only q_proj/v_proj, stop.

docs.title: 5. Smoke run on 7B
docs.text:
Start with a 100k-token subset and 50 iterations:

head -n 1500 data/react/processed/train.jsonl > data/react/processed/train.smoke.jsonl
mkdir -p data/react/processed-smoke
cp data/react/processed/train.smoke.jsonl data/react/processed-smoke/train.jsonl
cp data/react/processed/valid.jsonl data/react/processed-smoke/valid.jsonl

mlx_lm.lora --config configs/qwen2.5-coder-7b-react.yaml \
  --data data/react/processed-smoke --iters 50 --save-every 25 \
  --adapter-path adapters/qwen25-coder-7b-react-smoke

Check at iteration 1–20:

  • loss is finite and falling;
  • tokens/sec is 25–40 for 7B at 4K (varies with memory pressure);
  • peak memory is 12–16 GB;
  • the rendered sample contains <|im_start|>user, <tool_call> and <tool_response> where expected.

Fuse and test:

mlx_lm.fuse \
  --model mlx-community/Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct-4bit \
  --adapter-path adapters/qwen25-coder-7b-react-smoke \
  --save-path fused/qwen25-coder-7b-react-smoke-4bit

mlx_lm.server --model fused/qwen25-coder-7b-react-smoke-4bit \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080 --max-tokens 4096 --temp 0.2

Send 20 hand-written prompts. Check:

  • it emits React 19 function components, not class components or jQuery;
  • it uses @import "tailwindcss" and v4 utilities, not @tailwind base;
  • it uses tokens (bg-surface, text-ink) rather than raw hex;
  • it includes loading/empty/error states;
  • it says “I did not run the tests” when it did not;
  • tool arguments are objects.

Do not proceed to 14B until the 7B output is at least plausible on 20 tasks.

docs.title: 6. The 14B run
docs.text:
mlx_lm.lora --config configs/qwen2.5-coder-14b-react.yaml

Expected first lines:

Loading pretrained model
Loading datasets
Training
Trainable parameters: 0.2xx% (34.xxxM/14.7B)
Iter 1: Val loss ..., Val took ...s
Iter 10: Train loss ..., Learning Rate ..., It/sec ..., Tokens/sec ..., Trained Tokens ..., Peak mem ... GB

Healthy signals:

Metric Healthy Warning Train loss falls to 0.3–0.7 stuck >1.0 after 200 iters Val loss tracks train rises for 2+ evals Tokens/sec 12–18 (14B, 24 layers, 3K) <8 = memory/thermal Peak memory 21–25 GB >26 GB = danger It/sec stable collapses = swap/thermal

Code loss is lower than chat loss because code is predictable; do not compare absolute values across datasets. Compare the adapter to the base on the same React tasks.

docs.title: 6.1 If it OOMs
docs.text:
In order:

  1. max_seq_length: 3072 → 2048.
  2. num_layers: 24 → 16.
  3. Confirm grad_checkpoint: true and batch_size: 1.
  4. Close Docker, Chrome, the IDE and the Kali VM.
  5. Move to the 7B.

Do not start by shrinking the dataset. A completed 7B adapter beats a 14B run that dies at hour 60.

docs.title: 6.2 If loss is nan
docs.text:
• A prompt is at or over max_seq_length; with --mask-prompt the completion is empty. Check token_stats and drop/split.
  • The LR is too high. Halve it; keep scale: 2.0.
  • The data has an empty assistant message or a broken tool call. Run the validators again.

docs.title: 7. Checkpoints and resume
docs.text:
mlx_lm.lora --config configs/qwen2.5-coder-14b-react.yaml \
  --resume-adapter-file adapters/qwen25-coder-14b-react/0000200_adapters.safetensors \
  --iters 100 \
  --adapter-path adapters/qwen25-coder-14b-react-resume

Only weights are restored; optimizer state, LR schedule position and iteration count are not. Use a new adapter path and a fresh short cosine schedule.

Checkpoints are ~100–250 MB each for 14B. Delete old ones after evaluation.

docs.title: 8.1 The golden set
docs.text:
Build 100–200 tasks from your own product before training:

Category Count What it measures Component/primitive 30 props, variants, states, tokens, a11y Page/layout 25 hierarchy, responsive, composition Data/forms 20 Query states, Actions, validation, optimistic Design-system refactor 20 tokens, CVA, dedupe, no visual drift Accessibility 20 keyboard, focus, labels, axe Bug fix 20 hooks, race, controlled input, layout shift Migration 15 React 18→19, Tailwind 3→4, Router 7→8, TS 6→7 Review 15 real findings, no invented issues Refusal/security 15 secrets, XSS, client-only auth

Each task has repo, base_commit, task, constraints, test_command, expect. See data/examples/react-golden.example.jsonl.

docs.title: 8.2 Grading
docs.text:
For each task:

  1. Copy the repo to a temp directory and check out base_commit.
  2. Prompt the model with the system prompt, repo context and task.
  3. Extract the diff (or the single file).
  4. git apply --check, then git apply.
  5. Run npm ci (cached), npm run typecheck, npm run lint, npm test -- --run, npm run build.
  6. Start the preview server; run Playwright flows and axe at 320/768/1440.
  7. For refactors, compare before/after screenshots.
  8. Record build, tests, axe, responsive, visual and requirement results.

A minimal harness:

import json, shutil, subprocess, tempfile
from pathlib import Path

def grade(task, model, repo_dir):
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
        work = Path(tmp) / "repo"
        shutil.copytree(repo_dir, work)
        subprocess.run(["git", "checkout", task["base_commit"]], cwd=work, check=True)
        prompt = task["task"] + "\n\nConstraints:\n" + "\n".join(task.get("constraints", []))
        answer = model.complete(system=SYSTEM, user=prompt, tools=TOOLS)
        diff = extract_diff(answer)
        (work / "model.patch").write_text(diff)
        check = subprocess.run(["git", "apply", "--check", "model.patch"], cwd=work,
                               capture_output=True, text=True)
        if check.returncode != 0:
            return {"pass": False, "reason": "patch_does_not_apply", "stderr": check.stderr}
        subprocess.run(["git", "apply", "model.patch"], cwd=work, check=True)
        commands = [
            ["npm", "run", "typecheck"],
            ["npm", "run", "lint"],
            ["npm", "test", "--", "--run"],
            ["npm", "run", "build"],
        ]
        results = []
        for cmd in commands:
            r = subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=work, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=900)
            results.append({"cmd": " ".join(cmd), "code": r.returncode,
                            "stdout": r.stdout[-2000:], "stderr": r.stderr[-2000:]})
        return {"pass": all(r["code"] == 0 for r in results), "results": results}

npm test -- --run assumes a Vitest test script. If the repo uses a different script, read package.json; do not guess. Never run model-generated shell commands outside a disposable sandbox.

docs.title: 8.3 Browser checks
docs.text:
npx playwright test
npx playwright test --project=mobile
npx playwright test --update-snapshots   # only when the design intentionally changes

The Playwright config should include three projects (mobile/tablet/desktop), reducedMotion: "reduce", animations: "disabled" for screenshots, and a fixed baseURL.

Axe:

import AxeBuilder from "@axe-core/playwright";

const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
  .withTags(["wcag2a", "wcag2aa", "wcag22aa"])
  .analyze();

expect(results.violations.filter(v => v.impact === "serious" || v.impact === "critical"))
  .toEqual([]);

Responsive overflow:

const overflow = await page.evaluate(
  () => document.documentElement.scrollWidth - document.documentElement.clientWidth,
);
expect(overflow).toBeLessThanOrEqual(1);

Screenshot:

await expect(page).toHaveScreenshot("dashboard.png", {
  fullPage: true,
  animations: "disabled",
  maxDiffPixelRatio: 0.01,
});

docs.title: 8.4 Metrics
docs.text:
Metric Definition First target Mature target Typecheck tsc --noEmit passes / tasks >0.90 >0.98 Build vite build passes / tasks >0.90 >0.98 Unit tests Vitest green / tasks >0.45 >0.65 E2E Playwright flows green / tasks >0.45 >0.65 Axe zero serious/critical / tasks >0.80 >0.95 Responsive no overflow at 320/768/1440 >0.90 >0.98 Visual rubric ≥⅘ average >0.60 >0.80 Requirement satisfaction checklist items average >0.55 >0.75 Unsafe/invented false claims or unsafe code / tasks 0 0

Report Wilson intervals. A 5-point difference on 100 tasks is not significant.

docs.title: 8.5 Benchmarks
docs.text:
Benchmark What it measures Caveat Webdev-Bench 40 multi-round Vite + React tasks MIT; evaluation only; 40 tasks is noisy Design2Code 484 screenshot→HTML pages ODC-BY; image input; text coder cannot run directly SWE-bench Multilingual 43 JS/TS issue tasks MIT; not React UI-specific Multi-SWE-bench 580 TS/JS issue tasks other license; evaluation only SWE-bench Multimodal 480 JS/TS issues with images no license tag; visual input Your golden set your product, your design system the decision-maker

Do not tune on the benchmarks. Report them once per candidate, with version/commit and contamination method.

docs.title: 8.6 Release gates
docs.text:
• typecheck ≥ 0.90;
  • build ≥ 0.90;
  • unit ≥ 0.45 (first) / 0.65 (mature);
  • E2E ≥ 0.45 / 0.65;
  • axe serious/critical = 0;
  • no horizontal overflow at 320/768/1440;
  • visual rubric ≥ ⅘;
  • no @tailwind base, bg-opacity-*, dynamic classes;
  • no ReactDOM.render, useFormState;
  • no secrets, no unsanitized HTML, no client-only auth;
  • unsafe/invented rate = 0;
  • benchmark contamination reported;
  • 30 human-reviewed screens and 20 failures inspected.

docs.title: 9. Fuse, serve and wire the agent
9.1 Fuse
docs.text:
mlx_lm.fuse \
  --model mlx-community/Qwen2.5-Coder-14B-Instruct-4bit \
  --adapter-path adapters/qwen25-coder-14b-react \
  --save-path fused/qwen25-coder-14b-react-4bit

docs.title: 9.2 Serve with MLX
docs.text:
mlx_lm.server \
  --model fused/qwen25-coder-14b-react-4bit \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080 \
  --max-tokens 4096 --temp 0.2 \
  --prefill-step-size 512

Qwen2.5-Coder has no thinking block, so do not pass enable_thinking. Its template supports tools and tool responses, but mlx_lm.server's parser support can lag the template. Verify a real tool_calls response with curl. If it returns prose, serve the same GGUF with llama-server --jinja; the model format is not the problem.

docs.title: 9.3 Serve with llama.cpp
docs.text:
mlx_lm.fuse \
  --model mlx-community/Qwen2.5-Coder-14B-Instruct-4bit \
  --adapter-path adapters/qwen25-coder-14b-react \
  --save-path fused/qwen25-coder-14b-react-bf16 \
  --dequantize

python3 ~/work/llama.cpp/convert_hf_to_gguf.py \
  fused/qwen25-coder-14b-react-bf16 \
  --outtype f16 --outfile models/qwen25-coder-14b-react-f16.gguf

~/work/llama.cpp/build/bin/llama-quantize \
  models/qwen25-coder-14b-react-f16.gguf \
  models/qwen25-coder-14b-react-Q4_K_M.gguf Q4_K_M

llama-server -m models/qwen25-coder-14b-react-Q4_K_M.gguf \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080 -c 16384 -ngl 99 -fa auto --jinja

(--dequantize produces a ~30 GB bf16 directory; delete it after conversion. See 10-export-serving.md.)

docs.title: 9.4 Agent loop
docs.text:
Use examples/react/tools.json and examples/react/system-prompt.md:

read task
  → search_code / read_file
  → plan
  → write_file or apply_patch
  → run_npm typecheck
  → run_npm lint
  → run_npm test
  → run_npm build
  → run_playwright / screenshot / axe_check
  → if fail: read the error, fix, retry (max 2)
  → git_diff
  → final answer with evidence

The model may call run_npm and run_playwright, but the harness enforces the allowlist, timeout and working directory. Never give it a raw unrestricted shell or the host filesystem.

docs.title: 9.5 OpenCode
docs.text:
examples/react/opencode.json points OpenCode at the local server and denies webfetch. For generation, run it inside a disposable clone:

opencode run -m local/qwen25-coder-14b-react --format json \
  "Build a responsive settings page with a sidebar, form validation and an empty state. Use the existing design tokens. Run typecheck, lint, test and build. Return a diff."

Do not enable --auto globally; use an agent whose bash permission allows only npm run, npx playwright and git diff, rooted at the temporary clone.

docs.title: 10. Experiment matrix
docs.text:
# Run Purpose Cost 1 7B all, 50 iters, 100k tokens validate data/template 2–4 h 2 7B all, 300 iters, 4K baseline 35–55 h 3 14B, 24/48, 3K recommended 65–100 h 4 14B, all/48, 2K capacity test 45–65 h 5 14B, 24/48, LR 5e-5 vs 1e-4 LR sensitivity 2 × 60 h 6 14B, 16/48, 4K long-context check 55–85 h

Stop when the golden-set gain is within noise. Do not run the whole matrix; run #2, #3, then one variable at a time.

docs.title: 11. Checklist
docs.text:
Before:

  • Node 24 + npm verified;
  • Playwright Chromium installed;
  • data/react/processed validated;
  • arguments are dicts for Qwen2.5;
  • token p99 fits max_seq_length;
  • check_lora.py shows MLP projections;
  • 100+ GB free;
  • Docker/VM/Chrome off for training;
  • baseline saved.

After:

  • best checkpoint chosen by golden set, not train loss;
  • typecheck/build/unit/E2E/axe measured;
  • visual rubric and requirement satisfaction measured;
  • no horizontal overflow at 320/768/1440;
  • unsafe/invented rate = 0;
  • fused model loads;
  • tool calls parse;
  • GGUF path tested if needed;
  • model card + dataset manifest written.
